searchText: Makes sense to me. May be have validator supernodes + non-validator full nodes (probably with a larger custody like 16-32 subnets)? I think it depends on *why* the devnet is non functional today. ==> Will it help to have supernodes only? It may not have anything to do with there being non supernodes, but it seems hard to be sure, and it's certainly strictly easier to get something working with only supernodes, as a whole category of possible problems is avoided. Like, to me it feels beneficial to just resolve any bugs that have nothing to do with partial availability, and once that's settled then move on to figuring out partial availability, with the knowledge that any new problem that shows up is most likely due to it Hey <@466006586477772831> I've noticed this metric failing `data column sidecars verified for gossip` https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/f3a5e256da6f18fd019478c66419f6f07d98d64d/beacon_node/beacon_chain/src/beacon_chain.rs#L2148 I guess because everything is failing, as shown on the "Column processing failures" chart on the right. I've found a few issues with out node on devnet-3 (mostly single block lookup related), but haven't got a chance to look deeper or fix them yet <@498331483732312075> Grandine is 0 for both metrics, at least for supernodes For us most issues are related to our sync logic and recoverability from forks. I think it *may* relate to the numbers of supernodes but we just need to look into why LH is non functional today like Manu said - will try to find some time this week, sorry I've been a bit behind with devnets with other stuff going on rn which metrics did you refer to? `beacon_data_column_sidecar_processing_requests_total`, `beacon_data_column_sidecar_processing_successes_total` And I see only supernodes With out Teku current split (full v.s. super nodes) it would definitely help. I would also may assume that we may end up with a solution when a validating node _must_ be a supernode At least in theory there's no reason why this should be the case, unless reconstruction is not fast enough. And even if it were not fast enough, this should only have a small effect in a network where *most* of the stake is held by nodes that download everything. Most proposals and most attesting weight would behave as if there was no sampling, and there should only be temporary deviations of full nodes which are quickly resolved as soon as reconstruction happens. The network has 33.333...% of super nodes, 66.666...% of full nodes. In the [devnet](https://dora.peerdas-devnet-3.ethpandaops.io/forks), 33.333...% (6/18) of synced nodes are super nodes. I'm not sure if it can prove anything, but at least the proportion of synced super nodes wrt. synced full nodes is exactly the same than the proportion of super nodes wrt. full nodes in the network.
